mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES remains depressed while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, weekday errands and discretionary shopping shift toward home-based substitution, keeping RETAIL_REC below the prior four-week average over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean over the next 28 days while WORKPLACES stays near or below its current low level and RESIDENTIAL does not fall.

mechanism_narrative: A weekly rebound in GROCERY_PHARM indicates routine out-of-home trips are recovering; that spillover should lift adjacent discretionary shopping demand and push RETAIL_REC higher within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises by at least 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 14 days after a 5-point or larger weekly rise in GROCERY_PHARM.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES signals renewed commuting intensity; that increases passing exposure to retail corridors and should raise RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the next 28 days even as TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both trend upward.

mechanism_narrative: A positive PARKS shock diverts discretionary time toward outdoor recreation instead of indoor retail, so RETAIL_REC falls over the following week when PARKS is above its recent range.
candidate_trigger: PARKS crosses from negative to positive and stays above 0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the week after PARKS turns positive and remains above zero.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT drops sharply while RESIDENTIAL rises, mobility is being reallocated into stay-at-home behavior and fewer shopping trips, which lowers RETAIL_REC over the next month.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -15 while RESIDENTIAL exceeds +5
evidence_refs: fact:transit was -18.1 at t-1w while residential was +6.1
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall below its last-4-week mean within 28 days after TRANSIT is below -15 and RESIDENTIAL is above +5.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in WORKPLACES after a prior trough restores weekday foot traffic and lunch-time purchases, so RETAIL_REC increases in the next two weeks even if other categories are mixed.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES increases by at least 10 points from the prior week after being below -25
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within 14 days after WORKPLACES rebounds by 10 points or more from a sub -25 reading.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC rise together while PARKS is also positive, households are in an active-outing mode that spills from errands into shopping, lifting RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not remain above its prior four-week average over the next 28 days when GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS are both elevated.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in PARKS accompanied by weak TRANSIT indicates leisure substitution away from city-center shopping, so RETAIL_REC softens over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:parks turned positive at t-1w and stayed positive at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next 28 days despite PARKS staying positive and TRANSIT remaining below its recent average.
